newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Costello says no introduction of deposit insurance.
newsitem.headline: Costello says no introduction of deposit insurance.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday the government would not introduce compulsory deposit insurance for bank deposits with the emphasis to be put on prudential regulation of the banking industry.

"There is not going to be any depositor insurance. The safty net that will be applied will be prudential requirements," Costello said at a news conference following the release of the Wallis inquiry report into the financial system.
The inquiry considered the option of whether a U.S.-style compulsory deposit insurance sheme should be set up to cope with depositor claims in the event a bank collapses.
It did not, however, recommend the introduction of deposit insurance.
Many customers assume, incorrectly, that the government guarantees bank deposits.
